title: Cuero senior Taylor Martin crowned new Texas High School Rodeo Queen - NewsBreak
text: ABILENE, Texas - Last week, a new Texas High School Rodeo Queen was crowned: Cuero High School senior Taylor Martin. Martin competed against girls from high schools across all regions of Texas and made history as the first queen ever to record a perfect score on the horsemanship test. Horsemanship isn’t the only category scored in the competition. Other categories include a personal interview, a prepared speech, an impromptu question, a written test, modeling, personality, and appearance. Horsemanship, the personal interview and the prepared speech are each worth 50 points, while the other categories are worth 25 points each. Among all the categories, Martin said her favorite was horsemanship and explained why. “With taking the test, I had to know everything from the Texas High School Rodeo rule book. I did get a perfect score, and that hasn’t been done in a long time. I’m very proud of this accomplishment,” Martin said. In addition to excelling in horsemanship, Martin also enjoys the fashion side of rodeo events and described her favorite outfit. “We do have to wear a western dress. Mine is a leather dress from top to bottom, sequined and bedazzled in blue,” Martin said. Taylor’s mom and coach, Lisa Martin, said she’s proud that these competitions have helped her daughter and many other girls develop valuable life skills. “The Queen contest does so much for these girls. It’s not just a beauty pageant. It teaches them public speaking and how to network with others,” Lisa Martin said. Taylor has loved rodeos and horses since she was little, and she continues to enjoy the thrill of it all. “Anything that has to do with horses, I love to get my hands on. It’s helped me build my confidence in the process,” Taylor Martin said. Taylor will be back in action at nationals in Wyoming this July and hopes more girls across Texas will take part in Queen Rodeo Pageants.
